source.title: Latent Space Translation via Inverse Relative Projection
source.authors: Valentino Maiorca; Luca Moschella; Marco Fumero; Francesco Locatello; E. Rodolà

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether representations from different encoders can be translated and used for stitching, using inverse relative projection and downstream accuracy rather than a direct measurement of convergence with scale.
record.gate_note: The paper reports translation similarity, stitching accuracies, and qualitative sensitivity results. Scale-invariance experiments and cited prior findings about representation similarity do not themselves test the listed convergence versions, so they are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The paper proposes a mapping method (inverse relative projection, IRP) and reports how well one pretrained encoder's space translates into another's. That bears directly on V4, which names relative representations and stitching. The results are reconstruction cosine similarity and zero-shot stitched classification accuracy. Nothing tests scale, seeds, features or alignment metrics.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors present IRP as a method contribution for zero-shot latent translation and model reuse, enabled by inverting relative representations, decoder scale invariance, and Gaussian embedding-scale distributions. They report it works across encoders, languages and modalities. They do not frame it as a test of representational convergence. They list anchor count and parallel-anchor availability as open limitations.
record.recipe_differences: Uses inverse relative projection through a shared relative space, semantic anchors, anchor pruning/completion, and downstream stitching; it is not a scale sweep or a direct test of convergence with model size.
record.method_sensitivity: Reconstruction similarity depends on the anchor-pruning threshold δ and number of subspaces ω; the paper describes stronger inter-space results with medium-high pruning and high resampling.

fits_no_version.finding: Pretrained encoders share a unimodal Gaussian distribution of embedding norms, and downstream classifiers are largely invariant to rescaling their inputs (Figures 2, 4, 5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Different pretrained encoders differ mainly by an angle-preserving transform plus a rescaling that decoders tolerate.

fits_no_version.finding: In cross-modal stitching on N24News, text encoders are stronger source spaces than vision encoders (Figure 7).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Mappability between models is asymmetric and depends on how general the source model's pretraining domain is.

record.problems: No model-size or capability scaling test. Table 2 reports aggregate stitching performance and shows losses relative to non-stitch references. Some sensitivity and cross-domain results are presented only in figures, whose precise values are not available in the extracted text.
record.rows_left_out: No result-bearing rows were omitted. Figure 2 and Figure 4 scale-invariance results are outside the listed convergence versions.

untested.parts: No sweep over model size or capability.
Cross-modal stitching is reported only in a figure. There is no test of image-caption alignment rising as models improve.
No comparison across seeds of the same architecture.
Only IRP with parallel semantic anchors is tested. Linear or Procrustes maps, trained stitching layers, and mapping without paired data are not tested.
No interpretable features, neurons or SAE features are compared.
No alternative similarity measures and no out-of-distribution inputs. The δ/ω sweeps are settings of the method, not of an alignment metric.
No test of plateaus or of causes of alignment.

missing.what: Mean cosine between different sentences: 0.93 ± 0.05 in English absolute space and 0.98 ± 0.03 in XLM-R. These are the needed baselines for r2–r6.
TREC sensitivity analysis: Pearson r=0.7 between reconstruction similarity and accuracy; few anchors with a low condition number perform best.
Per-pair cross-modal stitching accuracies, which are only shown as a heatmap.

record.verdict_notes: Many comparator rows (absolute and non-stitch) were relinked to none because they are baselines or upper bounds for the zero-shot rows. The Table 2 NLP 'available' count of 20 for 4 encoders is unexplained in the text. The method requires parallel semantic anchors, so it does not speak to mapping without paired data.

versions.untested_parts: No sweep over model size or capability, and no test of whether alignment rises with scale.
N24News has associated text and images, but the paper does not test paired image-caption alignment rising as both models improve.
Averaging results over random seeds is reported, but the paper does not compare learned features or subspaces across independently initialized models of the same architecture.
Tests inverse-relative-projection translation with semantic anchors and downstream stitching; does not test the other mapping methods named in the claim or mapping without paired semantic anchors.
No comparison of recurring interpretable features, neurons, circuits, or SAE features.

Does not compare alternative similarity measures or test out-of-distribution inputs. It varies pruning and subspace hyperparameters, but these are not tests of similarity-measure settings as specified by this version.
Does not test whether partial alignment plateaus, or whether shared training data or objectives explain alignment.
